subject.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps

question: Should classic macOS onboarding scan installed applications and send their names to the configured model and ClawHub by default without a prior consent prompt?
rationale: The PR explicitly treats consent timing and default enablement as a product choice involving local inventory disclosure; code correctness cannot authorize that policy.

options.title: Require prior consent
options.body: Ask before scanning or transmitting application names while retaining recommendations for users who opt in.

options.title: Accept default-on scanning
options.body: Keep the proposed behavior with disclosure during scanning and the configuration kill switch.

options.title: Remove inventory recommendations
options.body: Keep plugin and skill discovery manual and omit installed-app inference from core onboarding.

recommendation.title: Require prior consent
recommendation.body: Ask before scanning or transmitting application names while retaining recommendations for users who opt in.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows broad involvement in this onboarding surface, and the PR itself frames the unresolved consent behavior as an intentional product choice.
